title: Proxy

act2.summary: access control added, with zero edits to caller or subject

solutions.title: One VehiclePositionProxy, shared by every caller
solutions.tradeoff: VehiclePositionProxy implements the same VehiclePositionService interface the real service does, so neither caller can tell it's there - caching and, later, access control both land in this one file instead of in every caller. The price: nothing but discipline stops a caller from bypassing the proxy and talking to the real service directly, and for a cheap-to-call subject the indirection is pure cost until a second concern like act 2's shows up to justify it.

reviewFocus: Do dashboard.ts and vehicle-position-cli.ts import RealVehiclePositionService at all, or only VehiclePositionService?
If a third caller constructed RealVehiclePositionService directly, would anything - the compiler, a test - catch that it bypassed the restriction?
Is WALKTHROUGH.md honest about which GoF proxy sub-pattern act 1 built (virtual/remote) versus which act 2 added (protection), and that both live in one class?
Given how cheap RealVehiclePositionService is to call, would this drill's situational verdict still hold if the real subject were actually slow or resource-limited?
